raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Cool Pacific air rushing through the Pismo Gap drops Edna Valley temperatures just enough to keep Grenache from turning flabby. Tolosa captures that shift in the 1772 bottling, trading the grape’s typical jammy weight for bright acidity and a tighter tannic frame.",
  "wine_summary": "Tolosa built its reputation on Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, so their approach to Grenache leans heavily into cool-climate restraint rather than heavy extraction or new oak. The 1772 label pulls fruit from older Edna Valley blocks where vines push roots through fractured volcanic tuff and clay loams. That soil composition limits vigor, naturally lowering yields and concentrating flavor without the need for aggressive canopy manipulation. You get the classic strawberry and white pepper notes, but they sit on a leaner backbone that reads closer to a Northern Rhône Syrah than a sun-baked Paso Robles Grenache.",
  "terroir_expression": "The valley’s east-west orientation funnels marine fog inland, extending the hang time and preserving malic acid while sugars accumulate slowly. Positas and Diablo clay loams drain quickly, forcing the vines to work harder for water and pulling up distinct mineral signatures from the volcanic bedrock. In the glass, that translates to a savory, almost flinty undertone beneath the red cherry and raspberry, with tannins that feel more structured than usual for the variety because the cooler nights slow down phenolic ripeness.",
  "vinification_summary": "Fermentation happens in open-top vessels, which allows gentle cap management and limits harsh tannin extraction while preserving primary fruit. The team typically uses a portion of whole-cluster fermentation, a technique where intact grape stems are left in the fermenter to introduce natural tannins and lift the wine with herbal, slightly peppery compounds. After aging in neutral French oak for roughly ten to twelve months, the wine avoids the vanilla-heavy profile that often masks Grenache’s natural transparency.",
  "food_pairing": [
    "Nashville hot chicken cutlets cut through the wine’s moderate tannins while the cool-climate acidity wipes away the oil and chili heat.",
    "Braised lamb shanks with rosemary and garlic align with the wine’s dried herb and earthy undertones, letting the fruit bridge the rich meat.",
    "Grilled sardines on sourdough with lemon and smoked paprika work because the wine’s lower alcohol and bright edge won’t overwhelm a delicate, oily fish, and the mineral finish mirrors the char."
  ],
  "comparable_wines": [
    "Tablas Creek Esprit de Beaucastel — shares the same Central Coast cool-climate Grenache focus but sits at a higher price and heavier extraction level.",
    "Ridge York Creek Syrah — different grape entirely, but delivers that same restrained, savory, coastal-tannin structure at a similar drinking weight."
  ],
  "style_profile": "Medium-bodied dry red with moderate acidity, structured tannins, and a savory mineral backbone.",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink the 2021 vintage within the next three to five years to catch the primary fruit before the cooler-climate structure dries out. Store at 55°F with steady humidity to keep the cork from shrinking, as Grenache’s thinner skins make it prone to premature oxidation.",
  "value_assessment": "$45 to $55 retail. You’re paying a premium for Edna Valley fruit and Tolosa’s farming reputation, but the wine competes directly with Au Bon Climat’s Pinot Noirs and similar Central Coast Rhône blends in that bracket. It holds its weight because the site expression actually comes through, though casual buyers expecting plush, high-alcohol Grenache will feel shortchanged.",
  "market_position": "Wine directors at coastal California restaurants and specialty retailers stock this for diners who want red wine without heavy oak or high alcohol. It lands on lists that pair with seafood and charcuterie, appealing to customers who usually drink Burgundy or Northern Rhône but want a domestic alternative.",
  "insider_take": "Skip this if you want a fruit-forward crowd-pleaser; the 13.8% ABV and cool-climate tannins demand a meal to open up. The real value here is how it proves Edna Valley can shape Grenache into something age-worthy instead of just another jammy Central Coast red.",
  "aging_potential_years": 7,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 2,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 9,
  "sensory": {
    "acidity": 4,
    "tannin": 3,
    "body": 3,
    "sweetness": 1,
    "alcohol": 2,
    "color_intensity": "medium",
    "aroma_intensity": "pronounced",
    "finish_length": "medium",
    "complexity": "complex",
    "quality_level": "very_good"
  }
}
